title: Hoping for Rightly Ordered Desires
author: O. Alan Noble
source: You Are Not Your Own Substack, December 5, 2025
summary: Noble addresses the spiritual maturity required to pursue good desires without entitlement. Even rightly ordered desires for friendship, marriage, children, or meaningful work are not guaranteed by God. The tension lies in acting hopefully while accepting denial. Noble draws on virtue ethics (endurance, courage, hope) to frame how believers navigate this paradox. Endurance sustains through rejection; hope enables action without presumption; prudence guides which goods to pursue. Culture pressures immediate gratification; Christian faith demands patient trust in divine will.
points: Good desires are not promises from God and require spiritual maturity.
Endurance and hope sustain believers through denial of rightly ordered goods.
Culture pressures immediate gratification while opposing biblical virtue and patience.
Prudent action toward good goals must coexist with trust in God.
Twin temptations of presumption and despair threaten those with unfulfilled desires.
quotes: You are not promised all that you desire, even when your desires are rightly ordered.
Endurance is the better part of courage because it takes more courage to endure suffering than to charge into battle.
Ask God for good gifts and believe that your Father will give them.

Hope enables us to rightly pursue those desires without falling into presumption or despair. Our Father will give us good gifts but sometimes that bread does not look like what we expect.” Archived from You Are Not Your Own Substack on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
